quality.question: My grey text on a white background looks faint, is that a problem?
quality.answer: Yes, it may be a contrast issue: WCAG 2.2 Level AA Success Criterion 1.4.3 requires text to have at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio, or 3:1 for large-scale text. [3] Grey text on white is not automatically a failure; check its contrast ratio against the background. [3]
searched: contrast ratio text on white background

quality.question: buttons too small?
quality.answer: At Level AA, WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.5.8 requires pointer targets to be at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels, unless an exception applies. [2] At Level AAA, Success Criterion 2.5.5 requires at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels, with its stated exceptions. [1] So buttons smaller than 24 × 24 CSS pixels may be too small for Level AA, but the spacing and other exceptions matter. [2]

quality.question: What contrast do large text and icons need?
quality.answer: For large text, WCAG 2.2 Level AA, SC 1.4.3 requires a contrast ratio of at least 3:1. [2] Level AAA, SC 1.4.6 requires at least 4.5:1. [1][3] Icons required to understand content need at least 3:1 under the technique for Level AA SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast. [4][5]

quality.question: What's the difference between 1.4.3 and 1.4.6?
quality.answer: WCAG 2.2 Level AA, **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)** requires a contrast ratio of at least **4.5:1** for text, or **3:1** for large-scale text. [1] Level AAA, **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced)** raises those thresholds to **7:1** for text and **4.5:1** for large-scale text. [2] Both criteria exempt incidental text and text that is part of a logo or brand name from contrast requirements. [1][2]

quality.question: Does disabled button text need good contrast?
quality.answer: No. WCAG 2.2 Level AA, Success Criterion 1.4.11, exempts inactive controls such as disabled buttons from its contrast requirement. [1][2]

quality.question: Does a logo need to meet contrast rules?
quality.answer: A logo is not specifically addressed by these sources, so I don’t know whether it needs to meet contrast rules. WCAG 2.2 Level AA Success Criterion 1.4.11 requires meaningful graphics to achieve 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors, but the sources don’t say whether a logo is covered by that requirement. [2][5]

quality.question: Which success criteria are new in WCAG 2.2?
quality.answer:
The new WCAG 2.2 success criteria are:

- **Level A:** 3.2.6 Consistent Help; 3.3.7 Redundant Entry. [2]
- **Level AA:** 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum); 2.5.7 Dragging Movements; 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum); 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum). [2]
- **Level AAA:** 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced); 2.4.13 Focus Appearance; 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced). [2]

quality.question: Is 4.1.1 Parsing still required?
quality.answer: No. WCAG 2.2 removed Success Criterion 4.1.1 Parsing, so it is no longer a WCAG 2.2 requirement; it was originally a Level A criterion. [1][2] If you must conform to WCAG 2.0 or 2.1, you may still need to test and report it. [3]

quality.question: At what width must content reflow without horizontal scrolling?
quality.answer: For **WCAG 2.2 Level AA, Success Criterion 1.4.10 (Reflow)**, vertically scrolling content must reflow at a width of **320 CSS pixels** without requiring horizontal scrolling to read lines of text. [3]

quality.question: How many times per second can content flash?
quality.answer: **WCAG 2.2 Level A, Success Criterion 2.3.1**: Content must not flash more than three times in any one-second period, unless the flash is below the general flash and red flash thresholds. [1]

quality.question: Can I use a puzzle CAPTCHA on my login page?
quality.answer: Yes. WCAG 2.2 Level A, Success Criterion 1.1.1, allows CAPTCHA, but requires text alternatives that identify and describe its purpose and alternative CAPTCHA forms using different sensory output modes. [1] WCAG 2.2 Level AAA, Success Criterion 3.3.9, additionally says a cognitive function test such as solving a puzzle must not be required for authentication unless an alternative authentication method or assistance mechanism is available. [3]

quality.question: Quel est le contraste minimum pour le texte ?
quality.answer: Au niveau AA, le critère 1.4.3 exige un contraste d’au moins 4,5:1 pour le texte, ou 3:1 pour le texte de grande taille. [1] Les exceptions incluent notamment le texte décoratif, celui d’un composant inactif et les logotypes, qui n’ont pas d’exigence de contraste. [1]
